services.title: Roof Replacement
services.shortDescription: Complete tear-off and professional installation of your new roof system.
services.fullDescription: A full roof replacement starts with stripping the old shingles down to the decking so we can inspect every square foot for rot, sagging, or water damage. We replace any compromised decking boards, install synthetic underlayment, ice and water shield in valleys and along eaves, new drip edge, and proper ridge vent ventilation before laying your chosen shingles. Most residential replacements on a standard home are completed in a few days, weather permitting. Options include asphalt architectural shingles, impact-resistant shingles (Class 3 and Class 4), and standing seam metal. Cost depends on roof size, pitch, material choice, and the number of layers being removed, and we'll walk you through it in a written estimate.

We repair hail damage, wind uplift, fallen tree damage, and flashing failures. If your roof needs a partial repair, we match existing shingles as closely as possible. If the damage warrants a full replacement, we walk you through the options.

Options include standard 3-tab shingles (budget-friendly), architectural/dimensional shingles (thicker and more wind-resistant), and impact-resistant shingles rated Class 3 or Class 4 (designed to stand up to hail, and in some areas eligible for insurance premium discounts). Every installation includes proper starter strip, synthetic underlayment, and hip and ridge cap shingles for a finished system.

services.title: Metal Roofing
services.shortDescription: Standing seam and corrugated metal roofing for maximum longevity, energy efficiency, and weather resistance.
services.fullDescription: Metal roofing is a long-term investment that pays off in durability, energy savings, and curb appeal. Options include standing seam panels (a concealed fastener system for a clean, modern look and strong weather resistance) and exposed-fastener corrugated or ribbed panels (cost-effective for agricultural buildings, shops, and budget-conscious homeowners). Standing seam metal roofs commonly last 40-70 years with little maintenance, reflect solar heat to reduce cooling costs, and are available with Class A fire ratings and Class 4 impact resistance. Materials include 24-gauge and 26-gauge steel with factory paint finishes, as well as aluminum for coastal environments. Metal roofing can often be installed over one existing layer of asphalt shingles, saving on tear-off costs.
keyPoints: Standing seam (concealed fastener) and corrugated (exposed fastener) options
Long lifespan with minimal maintenance
Reflects solar heat to help reduce cooling costs

services.title: Gutter Installation
services.shortDescription: Seamless aluminum gutters, gutter guards, and complete drainage solutions to protect your roof investment.
services.fullDescription: A new roof without proper drainage is only half the job. Seamless aluminum gutters are formed to the exact dimensions of your roofline, so there are fewer seams and fewer leak points. Standard 5-inch K-style gutters handle most residential homes; 6-inch oversized gutters are recommended for steep-pitch roofs or heavy rainfall areas, and half-round gutters suit historic or architectural homes. Downspouts are sized and positioned to direct water away from your foundation, with extensions or underground drainage tie-ins where needed. Gutter guard options include micro-mesh (best for pine needles and small debris), reverse-curve, and foam inserts.
keyPoints: Seamless aluminum gutters
5-inch standard and 6-inch oversized options

faq.question: What affects the cost of a new roof?
faq.answer: The main factors are roof size, pitch (steeper means more labor), the number of existing layers to tear off, material choice (3-tab, architectural, impact-resistant, or metal), and any decking repairs needed. We'll give you a written estimate for your roof.

faq.question: Does insurance cover roof replacement?
faq.answer: That depends on your policy and on what caused the damage. Many homeowner's policies cover sudden damage from events like hail, wind, or fallen trees, minus your deductible. Check your policy or ask your insurance agent about your coverage.

faq.question: How long does a roof replacement take?
faq.answer: The installation itself usually takes one to a few days for most residential homes. A simple single-story home with a walkable pitch might be done in a single day; a larger or steeper home with multiple layers to tear off takes longer. We'll give you a timeline for your project.

faq.question: What are the signs that my roof needs to be replaced?
faq.answer: Common signs include shingles that are curling, cracking, or missing; excessive granule loss (check your gutters for grit buildup); visible daylight or water stains in your attic; sagging areas on the roof deck; and a roof that's 20-25 years old. After a hailstorm, look for dents on gutters, downspouts, or AC units: if those are dented, your shingles likely took hits too. An inspection takes the guesswork out of it.

faq.question: What's the difference between architectural and 3-tab shingles?
faq.answer: 3-tab shingles are flat, uniform, and budget-friendly. Architectural shingles (also called dimensional or laminate) are thicker, more textured, and more wind-resistant. Most new installations today use architectural shingles.
